amstar2_items.justification: Research questions and eligibility criteria explicitly apply the PICO framework (Population: rural piped water utilities; Intervention: creative financing mechanisms; Comparison: conventional financing models; Outcome: sustainability measures), mapped in Abstract, Methods (p. 4), and Table 3 (p. 9).
No pre-registered review protocol (e.g., PROSPERO or OSF) or written a priori protocol is reported, and no protocol deviations are discussed.

Authors state they restricted inclusion to peer-reviewed journal articles for writing and review standards (p. 4), but do not explain or justify eligible empirical study designs (mixing LCCA, mixed-methods field studies, system dynamics simulations, descriptive case reports, and an existing systematic review of 97 articles).

Only a single database (Scopus) was searched (May 2024), restricted to English-language articles from 2009–2024, with no grey literature, reference list hand-searching, trial/study registries, or expert consultation.
Page 4 explicitly reports duplicate independent study selection: 'Screening was performed independently by two reviewers, with discrepancies resolved through discussion.'

Page 4 notes that data extraction captured study descriptors, financing mechanisms, and sustainability findings, without stating that extraction was performed independently in duplicate or verified by a second reviewer.
No list of full-text excluded studies with individual citations and exclusion reasons is provided anywhere in the article.

Tables 1–4 summarize authorship, country/setting, methods, populations, financing interventions, comparators, and outcomes, though sample sizes, data collection dates, and follow-up timeframes are missing for several included studies.

Authors applied a generic 5-item adapted CASP reporting checklist (clarity of aims, methodology appropriateness, intervention description, outcome reporting, data quality) rather than a valid risk-of-bias tool addressing confounding, selection bias, and measurement bias in non-randomized comparative studies; moreover, Table 5 contains unedited second-person prompt artifacts ('in your summary', 'in your description') based on secondary summaries rather than primary study appraisal.
The review discusses utility financing mechanisms, but does not report the research funding sources or sponsors of the 8 individual included studies.
No quantitative meta-analysis was performed; findings were synthesized narratively across heterogeneous study designs and metrics.

Although the Methods state that RoB judgments informed synthesis weighting, the Discussion does not incorporate study-level RoB into its causal claims, and the text (Abstract and p. 11: 5 Moderate, 3 Low) directly contradicts Table 5 (p. 12: 7 Moderate, 1 Low).

The review discusses contextual heterogeneity across countries and utility governance models (e.g., institutional capacity, rural income levels, regulatory maturity, and creditworthiness explaining varying financing effectiveness).
No quantitative meta-analysis was conducted, though the single-database English-only search creates substantial unexamined publication and indexing bias.
University grant funding is acknowledged on page 1, but no declaration of authors' competing interests or conflicts of interest is reported.

raw_response.methodological_notes: Substantive scope passes narrow Criterion 2 (examines tariff-setting regulations, prepaid vs. postpaid tariff rules, cross-subsidization, private/cooperative/community utility ownership and governance models in rural piped water supply). However, methodological quality under AMSTAR 2 is Critically Low due to multiple critical flaws (no registered protocol, single-database Scopus-only search yielding 49 hits and 8 included studies, no excluded-studies list, inadequate adapted-CASP RoB tool, and contradictory RoB integration). Forensic audit also reveals severe editorial/reporting defects: (1) p. 6 erroneously refers to 'the fifteen articles... presented in Table 2' whereas Table 2 and the entire review include 8 studies; (2) Abstract and p. 11 report 5 Moderate RoB and 3 Low RoB studies, contradicting Table 5 (p. 12), which rates 7 studies Moderate and only 1 (Grant et al., 2020) Low; (3) Table 5 contains unedited second-person LLM/reviewer prompt text ('in your summary is limited', 'acceptable in your description'); (4) the opening paragraph of the Discussion (p. 12) prints raw manuscript-template instructions verbatim; (5) Table 3 (p. 9) attributes ~15% coverage increase and >90% cost coverage from bank loans/cross-subsidy to Kumasi (2018) (duplicating Meleg 2012's outcomes), contradicting Table 4 (p. 10) which notes banks in Ghana granted zero loans to WSMTs; and (6) one of the 8 included studies (Walters & Javernick-Will, 2015) is itself a systematic literature review of 97 articles rather than a primary empirical study. Note that journal header prints Journal of People, Plants, and Environment (JPPE) rather than J Korean Soc Environ Eng.
